flawed_step: Step 2 of the proof attempt. Step 1: take a closed set C and a point x not in C. Step 2: apply normality to the disjoint sets {x} and C. That needs {x} to be closed, which is the T1 property, and the stated conventions explicitly leave T1 out. So this step cannot be justified, and no other route works either (see counterexample).
counterexample: Sierpinski space: X={0,1}, with open sets ∅, {1}, X. Its closed sets are X, {0}, ∅. Any two disjoint closed sets must include ∅, and such a pair is separated by the disjoint open sets ∅ and X. So X is normal. It is not regular: take C={0} and x=1. The only open set containing C is X, and X also contains x, so no disjoint open sets separate x from C.
assessment_summary: The usual proof that normal implies regular needs singletons to be closed (T1), and the definitions here explicitly drop T1. The proof breaks at that step. The Sierpinski space is normal under the given definition but not regular, so the statement is false.
